intended_object: The standard quaternion basis inside the Clifford algebra of the quadratic form Q(x,y) = c₁x² + c₂y² on R²: i = e₁, j = e₂, k = e₁e₂. These satisfy i² = c₁, j² = c₂, ij = k and ji = −k, which are the relations of ℍ[R, c₁, 0, c₂]. This reading comes from the docstring, the module section heading ("The clifford algebra isomorphic to the quaternions") and its use in `ofQuaternion`.
explanation:
The definition picks out i = ι(1,0), j = ι(0,1) and k = ij in Cl(Q c₁ c₂), where Q c₁ c₂ (v) = c₁·v₁² + c₂·v₂². It packages them as a `QuaternionAlgebra.Basis` with parameters (c₁, 0, c₂). Each relation checks out:
- i² = Q(1,0) = c₁.
- j² = Q(0,1) = c₂.
- ij = k holds by definition.
- ji = 0·j − k = −k holds because e₁ and e₂ anticommute: ij + ji equals the polar form of (1,0) and (0,1), which is 0 since Q has no cross term.

So this is the standard identification of the even/odd generators of a rank-2 Clifford algebra with a quaternion basis. It is the data that `liftHom` turns into the algebra map ℍ[R,c₁,0,c₂] → Cl(Q), which is one half of `CliffordAlgebraQuaternion.equiv`.

It is a specific object stated over an arbitrary commutative ring R with arbitrary parameters c₁ and c₂. Quaternion algebras with a zero middle parameter, ℍ[R,c₁,0,c₂], are exactly what diagonal binary forms give, so there is no narrowness issue. Mathlib has no separate declaration of this same basis.

The definition could also be read as an auxiliary bundle used only to build `ofQuaternion`, which would make `not_a_mathematical_object` defensible. I chose `faithful` because the basis is itself a standard mathematical object and is formalized correctly.
